takeaway: CHOP is the historical anthracycline regimen, but outcomes are poor except in ALK-positive anaplastic large-cell lymphoma. For CD30-positive disease, brentuximab vedotin plus CHP is a standard of care [1].
clinicalQuestion: What is standard first-line treatment for peripheral T-cell lymphoma, and where does brentuximab fit?
background: Peripheral T-cell lymphomas are biologically heterogeneous and respond poorly to conventional chemotherapy [1].
studyDesign: Narrative review of pathogenesis and treatment.
intervention: CHOP, and brentuximab vedotin plus CHP when CD30 is positive.
comparator: CHOP across subtypes that do not share the ALK-positive outlook.
mainFindings: Anthracycline regimens such as CHOP (cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisolone) have been the traditional treatment. Except for ALK-positive anaplastic large-cell lymphoma, outcomes are poor in most subtypes. The ECHELON-2 trial led to approval of brentuximab vedotin, an anti-CD30 antibody-drug conjugate. Combined with CHP (cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, and prednisolone), it has become a standard of care for CD30-positive peripheral T-cell lymphomas. Even with newer first-line combinations, outcomes for non-anaplastic subtypes remain extremely poor [1].
clinicalMeaning: Test for CD30 and for ALK. Do not expect CHOP to perform in PTCL as it does in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, apart from ALK-positive ALCL [1].
limitations: Response percentages from ECHELON-2 are not restated because they were not in the sentences used [1].
bottomLine: ALK-positive ALCL is the exception to poor CHOP outcomes. CD30-positive disease is treated with brentuximab plus CHP [1].
practiceImplication: Omit vincristine when brentuximab is added, because the regimen is CHP, not CHOP, in this review [1].
trustRationale: Current open review naming the regimen change. Trial numbers are not reproduced beyond the approval statement.
whatNotToOverclaim: Do not invent the ECHELON-2 hazard ratio.
